messages:
Nora: Quick check-in on pack coordination after the RFC — we need a clear operational model for core affinity + micro-sweeps. My concern: aggressive packing on the fastpath cores caused jitter in staging yesterday.

Diego: Saw that. The sweep task was pinned to the same worker pool as RPC dispatch. We should separate compaction workers and give them very low niceness.

Sam: Separation helps but we still hit interference because compaction touches the KV cache and forces CPU work to materialize cache pointers. Two ideas: 1) limit compaction to idle cores, 2) run compaction as cooperative, yielding after N windows.

Priya: Cooperative sounds safer. I prototyped a yield-based loop that does at most X tokens per yield. Pseudocode: 

```
while more_windows and tokens_processed < budget:
  compact_single(window)
  tokens_processed += window.tokens
  if tokens_processed >= yield_threshold:
    sched_yield()
```

This gave much smaller p99 blips in my run.

Diego: Nice. We should combine that with core-affinity hints so compaction prefers cores marked "background" by the scheduler. Also track compaction_cpu_ms in telemetry.

Nora: Agreed. Another operational concern: if packing moves requests into different micro-batches the billing and cost-aware routing numbers change. We need a pack_factor metric surfaced to the planner. If pack_factor delta > 15% trigger a planner re-score.

Sam: We already discussed pack_ratio elsewhere; I'd add cluster-level and tenant-level variants. For low-volume tenants pack_factor noise will be high so use an EWMA.

Priya: On KV interactions: compaction that merges windows across tenants can kick out pinned KV entries. Proposal: treat pinned_kv_hits as a safety signal. If pinned_kv_evictions > threshold, reduce compaction aggressiveness for that shard.

Diego: Good signal. We can reuse the existing headroom accountant as a global budget for background tasks: compaction consumes headroom credits; when low it backs off. That unifies admission.

Nora: Love the unified budget idea. Let's also expose a Console toggle (global + cluster) and a realtime compaction backlog chart for oncall. ops-bot could post alerts if backlog > X minutes and p95 rises.

Priya: small implementation note: compaction should be idempotent and safe to preempt. Use a write-intent marker on a window, so an interrupted compaction can resume without double-merge.

Sam: Also record "compaction.context" tags (mode: local/cross, core_affinity: background/any, reason: scheduled/manual) so we can correlate regressions.

Diego: Experiment idea: run cross-shard pack on a tiny fleet subset (10% dedicated nodes) with cooperative yields and background affinity. Measure p50/p95, token-cost delta, and pinned_kv_evictions.

Nora: OK action list: 1) Priya -> implement yield-based micro-compact & idempotent markers + pinned_kv_eviction metric. 2) Diego -> add background-core hints + integrate compaction with headroom credits. 3) Sam -> add pack_factor EWMA and planner hook for re-score. 4) Nora -> Console toggle + backlog chart + ops-bot alert rule.

ops-bot: CI: compaction/proto branch build queued (PR #4732). Tests run on small instances. Results will be posted here.

Sam: I'll take the planner work.

Priya: Taking the prototype patch.

Diego: I'll own the scheduler hint bits and headroom integration.

Nora: Great — let's reconvene after the prototype run. If anyone hits a regression, ping #eng-oncall ASAP. :thumbsup:
